what.text: Topiramate is an anti-seizure drug. As Topamax it is approved for epilepsy and for preventing migraine. For weight, it is approved only in one capsule with phentermine, sold as Qsymia.
How it acts, according to the FDA label

items.text: The label says the exact way topiramate acts in epilepsy and migraine is unknown. Lab studies found 4 actions: it blocks certain sodium channels, increases the activity of the calming signal GABA at some receptors, blocks a type of glutamate receptor, and inhibits the enzyme carbonic anhydrase.
Weight loss and loss of appetite are listed among the common side effects in its epilepsy and migraine trials. The label does not explain how it lowers weight.

research.text: Two large trials tested topiramate alone for weight in the early 2000s. The sponsor stopped the larger one early to develop a new formulation, and topiramate alone was never approved for weight. Later trials tested it with phentermine, which led to Qsymia.

research.title: Topiramate dose-ranging for weight, 385 adults, 6 months (Bray et al.)

facts.v: randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, dose-ranging trial: placebo or topiramate 64, 96, 192 or 384 mg/day
385 healthy obese adults aged 18 to 75; all in the same lifestyle program

research.found: Weight fell 2.6% on placebo and 4.8% to 6.3% on topiramate. The most frequent side effects were tingling, sleepiness and trouble with memory, concentration and attention. 21% on topiramate and 11% on placebo stopped because of side effects.

src.label: Bray GA, et al. Obes Res 2003

research.title: Topiramate for weight, 1,289 adults, planned 2 years (Wilding et al.)

facts.v: randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial: placebo or topiramate 96, 192 or 256 mg/day
1,289 adults aged 18 to 75 with BMI 30 to 50, or 27 to 50 with controlled high blood pressure or high blood fats
planned 2 years; the sponsor ended it early. Efficacy was analysed in 854 people who could reach 1 year
percent weight change; blood pressure; glucose; side effects

research.found: At 60 weeks, weight fell 1.7% on placebo and 7.0%, 9.1% and 9.7% on the 3 topiramate doses. Side effects were mostly nervous-system effects: tingling, poor concentration, depression, memory and language problems, nervousness and slowed thinking.

src.label: Wilding J, et al. Int J Obes 2004

research.title: Topiramate alone, phentermine alone, both, or placebo, 28 weeks (Aronne et al.)

facts.v: randomized, controlled trial with 7 arms, including topiramate ER 46 or 92 mg alone
obese adults; all had lifestyle counselling
percent weight loss; share losing at least 5%; memory and attention tests

research.found: Losing at least 5% of body weight: 15.5% on placebo, 39.2% and 48.6% on topiramate alone, and 62.1% and 66.0% on the combination. Testing found a problem only with attention.

research.title: Qsymia 1-year trials, 3,754 adults (Studies 1 and 2 in the label)

facts.v: 1,267 adults with BMI 35 or more, and 2,487 adults with BMI 27 to 45 and at least 2 weight-related conditions
percent weight change and share losing at least 5% at week 56

research.found: On the full-strength combination, weight fell 10.9% and 9.8%, compared with 1.6% and 1.2% on placebo. 40% and 31% of people left before week 56.

us.text: Topiramate is FDA approved, by prescription, as Topamax for epilepsy and migraine prevention. For weight, the only approved product is Qsymia, which combines it with phentermine. Using topiramate alone for weight is off-label. As of November 1, 2026.

items.text: Topamax tablets were approved December 24, 1996 as a new molecular entity (NDA 020505); Topamax Sprinkle capsules followed on October 26, 1998 (NDA 020844). The current label covers seizures from age 2 and migraine prevention from age 12.

Qsymia (phentermine and extended-release topiramate) was approved July 17, 2012 (NDA 022580) for long-term weight reduction with diet and exercise. Because of birth-defect risk, it is distributed only through certified pharmacies under the Qsymia REMS. The label calls for a pregnancy test before starting and every month in people who can become pregnant.
topiramate on its own is not approved for weight loss in the US. Using it that way is off-label.
topiramate is not a controlled substance. In Qsymia, the phentermine part is Schedule IV.

us.text: FDA says compounded drugs are not FDA approved. FDA does not check their safety, effectiveness or quality before they are sold.

world.lead: Topiramate is an approved prescription medicine for epilepsy and migraine in the US, Canada, the UK, the EU and Australia. The EU and UK now restrict its use in pregnancy with a pregnancy prevention programme. EMA refused the combination with phentermine in 2013. It is not on WADA's list.

countries.status: Approved medicine (Topamax 1996, epilepsy; migraine prevention). For weight, only in Qsymia (2012). Prescription-only.
Approved medicine: Topamax by Janssen, marketed since 1999. Prescription-only.

countries.status: Approved medicine (Topamax). Since June 2024 it must not be used in pregnancy, or by women who could become pregnant, unless the conditions of a Pregnancy Prevention Programme are met.

countries.status: Authorised nationally for epilepsy and migraine prevention. Since October 2023, a pregnancy prevention programme applies. EMA refused Qsiva (with phentermine) in 2013.
Approved medicine: TGA publishes product information for Topamax and generic topiramate. Prescription-only (Schedule 4).

after.text: European Union: in October 2023, the EU coordination group (CMDh) endorsed measures from EMA's safety committee because topiramate may raise the risk of neurodevelopmental problems in children exposed in the womb, on top of known birth defects. EMA says topiramate must not be used to prevent migraine or manage body weight during pregnancy. It also notes that in some EU countries topiramate is used with phentermine for weight reduction.

European Union: EMA's committee refused Qsiva in October 2012 and confirmed it in February 2013. Among its concerns were long-term psychiatric effects (depression and anxiety), memory and attention problems from topiramate, and harm to an unborn baby.

after.title: Sport
after.text: Topiramate is not named on the WADA 2026 Prohibited List or the 2027 List, and it is approved, so class S0 does not apply. Qsymia also contains phentermine, which is banned in competition (class S6.A).

side.text: Topiramate can harm an unborn baby, including cleft lip and palate. Its labels also warn of sudden eye problems, metabolic acidosis, kidney stones, mood changes, suicidal thoughts, and problems with memory, attention and speech.

items.text: first-trimester exposure raises the risk of major birth defects, including cleft lip and palate, and of babies being small for their age. Birth defects occurred in several animal species.
the UK MHRA also cites a possible higher risk of intellectual disability, autism spectrum disorder and ADHD in children of mothers who took topiramate in pregnancy.

src.label: MHRA Drug Safety Update, topiramate pregnancy prevention

items.text: sudden short-sightedness and secondary angle-closure glaucoma, which can lead to permanent vision loss; visual field defects.

too much acid in the blood (metabolic acidosis), kidney stones (1.5% of adults in epilepsy trials, 2 to 4 times the expected rate, higher in men), decreased sweating with overheating, and high ammonia.
antiepileptic drugs, including topiramate, about double the risk of suicidal thoughts or behaviour compared with placebo (0.43% vs 0.24% in pooled trials).
slowed thinking, trouble finding words, poor concentration and memory, depression and mood problems. The label warns about driving and operating machinery.

in migraine trials: tingling, loss of appetite, weight loss, altered taste, diarrhea, memory problems, numbness and nausea. In Qsymia trials: tingling, dizziness, altered taste, insomnia, constipation and dry mouth.
stopping suddenly can cause seizures, even in people without epilepsy.
in rats, topiramate did not affect male or female fertility. No human fertility studies were found.

unconfirmed: The year FDA approved Topamax for migraine prevention was not confirmed from FDA's record.
Which EU countries authorise a phentermine and topiramate product nationally was not checked.
surprises: EMA refused the phentermine and topiramate combination in 2013, yet EMA's 2023 topiramate review says that in some EU countries topiramate is used with phentermine for weight reduction.
